items.q: What gets scarcer as AI output gets cheap?
items.a: **Expert judgment and attention**—deciding what to do.

items.q: What's wrong with agents pinging leaders on their phones?
items.a: It spends **expert attention** on routine decisions; full automations **hide the complexity**.

items.q: What three buckets did expert review reveal?
Where did they spend as much time as on accuracy?
items.a: **Case routing**—pull unusual, undecided and critical cases out of the happy path.

items.q: How do you get busy experts to help with evals?
items.a: Bring them **filled-in examples** to react to, not a **blank spreadsheet**.

items.q: How did they reach three and a half nines?
items.a: Hill-climbing a clean critical set over **~1,000 evals they actually read**.
Only once a **random sample beat historic human work**.
**Scaled processes with material ROI** and written specs—not subjective judgment.
